5	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivDegree
6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.SchematicSupport
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.RigidPushforwardTransfer
8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.FlatteningStratificationUniversal
9	
10	/-!
11	# Pushing a divisor family down to the base, flatly
12	
13	Campaign milestone **D3'** (`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md:305`) asks
14	for the locus over which a Grassmannian `T`-point arises from a degree-`d`
15	`DivFamily` to be locally closed *universally*, by extending
16	`AlgebraicGeometry.flatLocusStratification_universal`
17	(`Picard/FlatteningStratificationUniversal.lean`) "to the family `C × G → G`".
18	
19	This file supplies the object that extension has to be about, and records why the
20	extension has to be phrased this way rather than by relativising the machine.
21	
22	## The shape of the reduction, and why it is forced
23	
24	`flatLocusStratification_universal` is stated for a module **on the base**,
25	`F : S.Modules`, with `π = 𝟙 S`. That is not an accident of its proof that a
26	later session can relax: the whole stratification machine is built on
27	`Scheme.Modules.pointRank : (X : Scheme) → X.Modules → ↥X → ℕ`, which takes a
28	module on *one* scheme and a point of *that* scheme. There is no relative
29	`pointRank` over a morphism, and `chartLocus`, `rankStratum`,
30	`isOpen_pointRank_pullback_eq` and `existsUnique_factor_rankStratum` all inherit
31	that shape. So a general-`π` universal property cannot be obtained by adding a
32	`π` to those statements; the family has to be *moved to the base* first.
33	
34	For a divisor family that move is available, and cheaply, because a relative
35	effective divisor is finite over the base — where a general proper family is not.
36	Concretely: `Scheme.Modules.HasProperSupport` is by definition
37	`IsProper (schematicSupportι F ≫ f)` (`Picard/QuotScheme.lean`), and
38	`DivFamily.properSupport` is exactly that datum for `f = pullback.snd π T.hom`.
39	A proper *quasi-finite* morphism is finite (`IsFinite.of_isProper_of_locallyQuasiFinite`),
40	hence affine, and `Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat` transfers along an affine
41	pushforward. Since `O_D` is the pushforward of its own restriction to the support
42	(`schematicSupportDescentIso`), the family's flatness over `T` becomes flatness of
43	`q_* O_D` over `T` *itself* — the `n = 0` shape the universal property consumes.
44	
45	## What is proved here, and what is assumed
46	
47	* `Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat.of_pushforward_of_isAffineHom` — the **converse** of
48	  `Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat.pushforward_of_isAffineHom`
49	  (`Picard/RigidPushforwardTransfer.lean`), which did not exist. Both directions
50	  are the same chart computation read in opposite directions; the content is that
51	  the two `Γ(T, U)`-module structures on `Γ(F, π ⁻¹ᵁ V)` agree, which is
52	  `Scheme.Hom.appLE_comp_appLE`.
53	
54	* `Scheme.DivFamily.coherentSheafFlat_id_pushforward` — for a divisor family whose
55	  divisor is quasi-finite over the base, `q_* O_D` is flat over `T` in the
56	  `CoherentSheafFlat (𝟙 T.left)` sense.
57	
58	**The quasi-finiteness is a hypothesis, not a theorem, and this file does not
59	pretend otherwise.** `LocallyQuasiFinite (schematicSupportι x.F ≫ pullback.snd π T.hom)`
60	says the divisor `D ⊆ X_T` has finite fibres over `T`. Mathematically it is
61	relative-dimension-1 content: on the curve fibre `C_t`, `D_t` is the zero scheme
62	of a regular section of an invertible ideal, hence `0`-dimensional. It has no
63	producer in this project, and `LocallyQuasiFinite` occurs nowhere else in
64	`Picard/`. It is stated as an instance binder so that a later producer discharges
65	every consumer at once.
66	
67	Worth recording for whoever prices the next step: this hypothesis is *cleaner*
68	than the one it replaces. `Picard/DivDegree.lean` gates its clopen degree
69	decomposition on `HasLocallyConstantDivDeg`, a `Prop`-class carrying local
70	constancy of `fiberDeg` as an assumption and also without a producer. With
71	quasi-finiteness instead, local constancy is downstream of a stratification
72	theorem rather than assumed beside it — the same missing geometry, but bought
73	once and in a form the machine can use.
74	
75	## What remains for D3'
76	
77	`flatLocusStratification_universal` has exactly **two** binders:
78	`[IsNoetherian S]` and `[F.IsFinitePresentation]`. `IsQuasicoherent` is a mathlib
79	instance *from* finite presentation, so it is not a separate requirement;
80	`DivFamily.isQuasicoherent_pushforward` below is kept because it is the cheap half
81	and is wanted in its own right, not because `:876` asks for it.
82	
83	Finite presentation of `q_* O_D` is `DivFamily.isFinitePresentation_pushforward`,
84	proved here. `isFinitePresentation_of_finite_sections`
85	(`Picard/RigidPushforwardTransfer.lean`) reduces it to `Module.Finite Γ(T,V)
86	Γ(q_* O_D, V)` on affine `V`, and that tower is:
87	
88	* `Module.Finite Γ(T,V) Γ(D,W)` for `W := (i ≫ q) ⁻¹ᵁ V`, from
89	  `IsFinite.finite_app` — this is where the finiteness of the support map is spent,
90	  and it is exactly what quasi-finiteness bought;
91	* `Module.Finite Γ(D,W) Γ(N,W)` from `finite_sections_preimage_of_isAffineHom`
92	  together with `isFinitePresentation_pullback_schematicSupportι`;
93	* the two compose by `Module.Finite.trans`, and the result transports back across
94	  `schematicSupportDescentIso` because `Γ(q_* F, V) = Γ(F, q ⁻¹ᵁ V)` and
95	  `Γ(i_* N, q ⁻¹ᵁ V) = Γ(N, (i ≫ q) ⁻¹ᵁ V)` are both `rfl`, and the native
96	  `Γ(T,V)`-action on `Γ(q_* F, V)` *is* `compHom` along `q.app V`, also `rfl`. The
97	  semilinearity is `Scheme.Modules.Hom.app_smul`.
98	
99	## What remains for D3'
100	
101	Two things, and neither is supplied here.
102	
103	**A stated bridge, not a free fit.** `:876` stratifies a module on the base and

134	/-- **Coherent-sheaf flatness descends along an affine pushforward** — the
135	converse of `Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat.pushforward_of_isAffineHom`.
136	
137	For affine `π : X ⟶ Y` over `p : Y ⟶ T`, flatness of `π_* F` over `T` gives
138	flatness of `F` over `T` along the composite. Read on an affine `V ⊆ Y`: the
139	sections of `π_* F` over `V` *are* `Γ(F, π ⁻¹ᵁ V)` definitionally, with `π ⁻¹ᵁ V`
140	affine because `π` is, and the two `Γ(T, U)`-module structures agree because
141	`(π ≫ p).appLE = p.appLE ≫ π.appLE`.
142	
143	Flatness on the preimage charts `π ⁻¹ᵁ V` of an affine cover of `Y` is what the
144	hypothesis gives directly; `flat_section_of_affine_cover` globalises it to every
145	affine pair of `X`, which is where quasi-coherence of `F` is used. -/
146	theorem Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat.of_pushforward_of_isAffineHom
147	    {X Y T : Scheme.{u}} (π : X ⟶ Y) [IsAffineHom π] (p : Y ⟶ T)
148	    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
149	    (h : Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat p ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward π).obj F)) :
150	    Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat (π ≫ p) F := by
151	  classical
152	  -- For each point of `X` pick an affine `V ⊆ Y` around its image together with an
153	  -- affine `U ⊆ T` above it; `π ⁻¹ᵁ V` is then affine because `π` is.
154	  have hchart : ∀ x : X, ∃ (V : Y.Opens) (U : T.Opens) (_ : IsAffineOpen V)
155	      (_ : IsAffineOpen U), π.base x ∈ V ∧ V ≤ p ⁻¹ᵁ U := by
156	    intro x
157	    obtain ⟨U, hUaff, hU, -⟩ :=
158	      exists_isAffineOpen_mem_and_subset (x := p.base (π.base x)) (U := ⊤) trivial
159	    obtain ⟨V, hVaff, hxV, hVU⟩ :=
160	      exists_isAffineOpen_mem_and_subset (x := π.base x) (U := p ⁻¹ᵁ U) hU
161	    exact ⟨V, U, hVaff, hUaff, hxV, hVU⟩
162	  choose Vc Uc hVc hUc hmem hle using hchart
163	  intro U₀ hU₀ V₀ hV₀ e₀
164	  refine flat_section_of_affine_cover (π ≫ p) F
165	    (fun x => π ⁻¹ᵁ Vc x) (fun x => (hVc x).preimage π)
166	    Uc hUc (fun x => ?_) (fun x => ⟨x, hmem x⟩) (fun x => ?_) hU₀ hV₀ e₀
167	  · -- `π ⁻¹ᵁ Vc x ≤ (π ≫ p) ⁻¹ᵁ Uc x`
168	    rw [Scheme.Hom.comp_preimage]
169	    exact fun z hz => hle x hz
170	  · -- the chart flatness, read off the hypothesis at `Vc x`
171	    have base := h (hUc x) (hVc x) (hle x)
172	    have hφ : ((π ≫ p).appLE (Uc x) (π ⁻¹ᵁ Vc x)
173	          (by rw [Scheme.Hom.comp_preimage]; exact fun z hz => hle x hz)).hom =
174	        ((π.app (Vc x)).hom).comp ((p.appLE (Uc x) (Vc x) (hle x)).hom) := by
175	      have h1 := Scheme.Hom.appLE_comp_appLE π p (Uc x) (Vc x) (π ⁻¹ᵁ Vc x)
176	        (hle x) le_rfl
177	      refine RingHom.ext fun r => ?_
178	      have h2 := congrArg
179	        (fun (φ : Γ(T, Uc x) ⟶ Γ(X, π ⁻¹ᵁ Vc x)) => φ.hom r) h1
180	      simp only [CommRingCat.hom_comp, RingHom.comp_apply] at h2
181	      rw [RingHom.comp_apply, Scheme.Hom.app_eq_appLE]
182	      exact h2.symm
183	    change @Module.Flat _ _ _ _ (Module.compHom Γ(F, π ⁻¹ᵁ Vc x)
184	      ((π ≫ p).appLE (Uc x) (π ⁻¹ᵁ Vc x) _).hom)
185	    rw [hφ]
186	    exact base

188	/-- **The pushforward of `O_D` is flat over the base itself.**
189	
190	For a divisor family `x` whose divisor is quasi-finite over `T`, the pushforward
191	`q_* O_D` along `q = pullback.snd π T.hom` is flat over `T` in the
192	`CoherentSheafFlat (𝟙 T.left)` sense.
193	
194	This is the `n = 0` shape, but **not literally what
195	`AlgebraicGeometry.flatLocusStratification_universal` asks for**: its antecedent
196	carries a pullback along the test morphism, which at `φ = 𝟙` is not reduced away.
197	The bridged form is `coherentSheafFlat_id_pullbackId_pushforward` below.
198	
199	Route: `x.properSupport` is `IsProper (i ≫ q)` by definition, so with
200	quasi-finiteness `i ≫ q` is finite, hence affine; `schematicSupportDescentIso`
201	presents `x.F` as `i_*` of its restriction to the support, whose flatness over
202	`T` follows from `x.flat` by the converse above; pushing forward along the affine
203	`i ≫ q` over `𝟙 T.left` and transporting along `pushforwardComp` gives the
204	claim. -/
205	theorem Scheme.DivFamily.coherentSheafFlat_id_pushforward
206	    {S X : Scheme.{u}} {π : X ⟶ S} {T : Over S} (x : Scheme.DivFamily π T)
207	    [LocallyQuasiFinite
208	      (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι x.F ≫ pullback.snd π T.hom)] :
209	    Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat (𝟙 (T.left : Scheme.{u}))
210	      ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj x.F) := by
211	  letI := x.isFinitePresentation
212	  haveI : x.F.IsQuasicoherent := inferInstance
213	  set q := pullback.snd π T.hom with hq
214	  set i := Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι x.F with hi
215	  -- `i ≫ q` is proper by the divisor family's own support datum, hence finite,
216	  -- hence affine.
217	  haveI : IsProper (i ≫ q) := x.properSupport
218	  haveI : IsFinite (i ≫ q) := IsFinite.of_isProper_of_locallyQuasiFinite _
219	  haveI : IsAffineHom (i ≫ q) := inferInstance
220	  haveI : IsAffineHom i :=
221	    inferInstanceAs (IsAffineHom (Scheme.Modules.annihilator x.F).subschemeι)
222	  -- present `O_D` as `i_*` of its restriction to the support
223	  set N := (Scheme.Modules.pullback i).obj x.F with hN
224	  have hdesc : x.F ≅ (Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj N :=
225	    Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportDescentIso x.F
226	  haveI : N.IsQuasicoherent := pullback_isQuasicoherent_hom i x.F inferInstance
227	  -- flatness of `i_* N` over `T`, transported from the family's flatness
228	  have h1 : Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat q ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj N) :=
229	    coherentSheafFlat_of_iso q hdesc x.flat
230	  -- descend it to `N` along the affine `i`
231	  have h2 : Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat (i ≫ q) N :=
232	    Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat.of_pushforward_of_isAffineHom i q N h1
233	  -- push forward along the affine `i ≫ q`, over the identity of the base
234	  have h3 : Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat (𝟙 (T.left : Scheme.{u}))
235	      ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (i ≫ q)).obj N) :=
236	    Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat.pushforward_of_isAffineHom (i ≫ q)
237	      (𝟙 (T.left : Scheme.{u})) N (by rwa [Category.comp_id])
238	  -- and identify `(i ≫ q)_* N ≅ q_* (i_* N) ≅ q_* O_D`
239	  intro U hU V hV eV
240	  exact coherentSheafFlat_of_iso (𝟙 (T.left : Scheme.{u}))
241	    ((Scheme.Modules.pushforwardComp i q).app N ≪≫
242	      (Scheme.Modules.pushforward q).mapIso hdesc.symm) h3 hU hV eV

244	/-- **`q_* O_D` is quasi-coherent** when the ambient family is proper.
245	
246	Free: properness of `π` gives `QuasiCompact` and `QuasiSeparated` of the projection
247	`q = pullback.snd π T.hom` by base change, and pushforward along a qcqs morphism
248	preserves quasi-coherence.
249	
250	Not a binder of `AlgebraicGeometry.flatLocusStratification_universal`, which asks
251	only for `[IsNoetherian S]` and `[F.IsFinitePresentation]` — quasi-coherence is a
252	mathlib instance from the latter. Kept because it is wanted in its own right and is
253	the cheap half of the pair. -/
254	theorem Scheme.DivFamily.isQuasicoherent_pushforward
255	    {S X : Scheme.{u}} {π : X ⟶ S} [IsProper π] {T : Over S}
256	    (x : Scheme.DivFamily π T) :
257	    ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj x.F).IsQuasicoherent := by
258	  letI := x.isFinitePresentation
259	  exact Scheme.Modules.pushforward_isQuasicoherent _ x.F

262	
263	`:876` asks, for a test morphism `φ : T' ⟶ S`, for
264	`CoherentSheafFlat (𝟙 T') ((Modules.pullback φ).obj F)`. At `φ = 𝟙` that is *not*
265	literally `coherentSheafFlat_id_pushforward`: the identity pullback is not reduced
266	away, so the carrier is `Γ((pullback (𝟙 T.left)).obj (q_* O_D), V)` where the
267	theorem above supplies `Γ(q_* O_D, V)`. This states the bridged form, so that
268	consumers do not have to rediscover which of the two shapes they hold.
269	
270	Note what this does and does not give: the `φ = 𝟙` **instance** of the antecedent,
271	not the antecedent as a family over all `φ`. -/
272	theorem Scheme.DivFamily.coherentSheafFlat_id_pullbackId_pushforward
273	    {S X : Scheme.{u}} {π : X ⟶ S} {T : Over S} (x : Scheme.DivFamily π T)
274	    [LocallyQuasiFinite
275	      (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι x.F ≫ pullback.snd π T.hom)] :
276	    Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat (𝟙 (T.left : Scheme.{u}))
277	      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (𝟙 (T.left : Scheme.{u}))).obj
278	        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj x.F)) := by
279	  intro U hU V hV eV
280	  exact coherentSheafFlat_of_iso (𝟙 (T.left : Scheme.{u}))
281	    (((Scheme.Modules.pullbackId (T.left : Scheme.{u})).app
282	      ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj x.F)).symm)
283	    x.coherentSheafFlat_id_pushforward hU hV eV

299	theorem Scheme.DivFamily.isFinitePresentation_pushforward
300	    {S X : Scheme.{u}} {π : X ⟶ S} [IsProper π] {T : Over S}
301	    [IsLocallyNoetherian (T.left : Scheme.{u})] (x : Scheme.DivFamily π T)
302	    [LocallyQuasiFinite
303	      (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι x.F ≫ pullback.snd π T.hom)] :
304	    ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj x.F).IsFinitePresentation := by
305	  letI := x.isFinitePresentation
306	  haveI := x.isQuasicoherent_pushforward
307	  refine Scheme.Modules.isFinitePresentation_of_finite_sections _ (fun V hV => ?_)

311	  haveI : IsFinite (i ≫ q) := IsFinite.of_isProper_of_locallyQuasiFinite _

314	  let D := Scheme.Modules.schematicSupport x.F

316	  let N : D.Modules := (Scheme.Modules.pullback i).obj x.F
317	  haveI : N.IsFinitePresentation :=
318	    Scheme.Modules.isFinitePresentation_pullback_schematicSupportι x.F x.isFinitePresentation

321	  letI : Module Γ(T.left, V) Γ(N, W) :=
322	    Module.compHom _ (Scheme.Hom.app (i ≫ q) V).hom
323	  haveI : Module.Finite Γ(T.left, V) Γ(D, W) := IsFinite.finite_app (i ≫ q) V hV

10	# B5 — semicontinuity of the fibrewise `h⁰`, both directions
11	
12	Campaign milestone **B5** (`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`): for
13	the constant curve `C_A = C ×_k Spec A` over a finitely generated
14	`k`-algebra `A` and an invertible sheaf `L` on `C_A`, the loci
15	
16	* `{t : Spec A | h⁰(C_t, L_t) ≤ n}` are **open**, and
17	* `{t : Spec A | n ≤ h⁰(C_t, L_t)}` are **closed**.
18	
19	Sources: Hartshorne III 12.8 (semicontinuity); Mumford, *Abelian
20	Varieties*, II §5 (the rank-of-minors argument on the two-term finite free
21	complex — the same engine as B3, which is why the plan files B5 "with B3");
22	Kleiman, *The Picard scheme* (FGA Explained), §5.
23	
24	## Statement audit (verdicts recorded BEFORE proving, per the campaign checklist)
25	
26	* **Honesty at stated generality**: upper semicontinuity of
27	  `t ↦ h⁰(X_t, F_t)` holds for any proper flat family with `F` coherent and
28	  flat over a **noetherian** base (Hartshorne III 12.8).  Here `X = C_A` is
29	  proper flat over `Spec A` (base change of the proper smooth `C/k`; a
30	  `k`-scheme is automatically flat over the field `k`) and an invertible `L`
31	  is coherent and flat over the base, so the pinned statement is TRUE for
32	  every finitely generated `k`-algebra `A` — the same noetherian pin as B3;
33	  milestone B2 extends consumers to arbitrary affine bases.
34	* **"Both directions" collapse (discrepancy note vs the plan's phrasing)**:
35	  for the ℕ-valued function `t ↦ h⁰(t)`, the two B5 directions are exact
36	  set-theoretic complements: `{n ≤ h⁰} = {h⁰ ≤ n − 1}ᶜ` (and `{0 ≤ h⁰}` is
37	  everything).  So a SINGLE gated direction (openness of the sublevel sets)
38	  yields the closed direction by `IsOpen.isClosed_compl` — proved
39	  unconditionally below (`isClosed_setOf_le_fiberH0`).  The plan's remark
40	  "the closed direction feeds B6 — D3 only pinned the open direction" is
41	  thereby discharged for free once the gate is.
42	* **No `h¹`-hypothesis**: unlike B3, semicontinuity needs no cohomological
43	  vanishing — only properness/flatness/coherence.  The gate must NOT carry
44	  a `FiberH1Vanishing` hypothesis (it would silently weaken every B6/J1
45	  consumer, which apply B5 precisely where `h¹` is unknown).
46	* **Vocabulary**: `h⁰` is `Scheme.Hom.fiberH0`
47	  (`Picard/RigidPushforward.lean`), the `κ(t)`-dimension of `Γ(C_t, L_t)` —
48	  the same pin as B3's rank, so B3's local-freeness conclusion and B5's

119	anywhere in the tree**; supplied as a hypothesis by consumers and discharged
120	by the B3/B5 session — the minors of the two-term finite free complex —
121	then deleted).  Content: `h⁰` upper semicontinuity over every finitely
122	generated `k`-algebra base.  The closed direction is NOT a separate field:
123	it is the set-theoretic complement, proved below
124	(`isClosed_setOf_le_fiberH0`). -/
125	class HasH0Semicontinuity (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) : Prop where
126	  /-- `h⁰` upper semicontinuity over every finitely generated `k`-algebra. -/
127	  upperSemicontinuity : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [Algebra.FiniteType k A],
128	    H0UpperSemicontinuity C A
129	
130	variable (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
131	variable (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [Algebra.FiniteType k A]
132	
133	/-- **B5, open direction** (extraction from the gate): `{h⁰(L_t) ≤ n}` is
134	open in `Spec A`. -/
135	theorem isOpen_setOf_fiberH0_le [HasH0Semicontinuity C]
136	    (L : (Limits.pullback C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).Modules)
137	    (hL : LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial L) (n : ℕ) :
138	    IsOpen {t : Spec (CommRingCat.of A) |
139	      (pullback.snd C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).fiberH0 L t ≤ n} :=
140	  HasH0Semicontinuity.upperSemicontinuity A L hL n
141	
142	/-- **B5, closed direction** (proved from the gate — the plan's "both
143	directions" collapse to complements for the ℕ-valued `h⁰`, see the module
144	docstring): `{n ≤ h⁰(L_t)}` is closed in `Spec A`.  This is the direction
145	milestone B6 consumes (closedness of the triviality locus
146	`{h⁰(L_t) ≥ 1} ∩ {h⁰(L_t⁻¹) ≥ 1}` in fibre degree 0). -/
147	theorem isClosed_setOf_le_fiberH0 [HasH0Semicontinuity C]
148	    (L : (Limits.pullback C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).Modules)
149	    (hL : LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial L) (n : ℕ) :
150	    IsClosed {t : Spec (CommRingCat.of A) |
151	      n ≤ (pullback.snd C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).fiberH0 L t} := by
152	  cases n with
153	  | zero =>
154	    have huniv : {t : Spec (CommRingCat.of A) |
155	        0 ≤ (pullback.snd C.hom
156	          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).fiberH0 L t} = Set.univ :=
157	      Set.eq_univ_of_forall fun t => Nat.zero_le _
158	    rw [huniv]
159	    exact isClosed_univ
160	  | succ m =>
161	    have hcompl : {t : Spec (CommRingCat.of A) |
162	        m + 1 ≤ (pullback.snd C.hom
163	          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).fiberH0 L t} =
164	        {t : Spec (CommRingCat.of A) |
165	          (pullback.snd C.hom
166	            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).fiberH0 L t ≤ m}ᶜ := by
167	      ext t
168	      simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_compl_iff, not_le]
169	      exact Nat.lt_iff_add_one_le.symm
170	    rw [hcompl]
171	    exact (isOpen_setOf_fiberH0_le C A L hL m).isClosed_compl
172	
173	end Scheme

9	/-!
10	# The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor
11	
12	This file constructs the **étale-sheafified relative Picard functor**
13	`Pic_{(C/k)ét}` of a smooth proper curve `C/k` and proves that it *is* a sheaf
14	for the étale topology — the object whose representability is the project's
15	central open obligation (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`).
16	
17	## Why the sheafification is the right object
18	
19	The relative Picard presheaf `T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`
20	(`Scheme.PicSharp.relPresheaf`, Kleiman §2 Def. `df:Pfs`) is in general **not
21	a sheaf** (Kleiman §2, L1330: "not *a priori* a sheaf"), and over a general
22	field it is **not representable** — the witness is Exercise `ex:Pfs`, the conic
23	`u²+v²+w²=0` in `ℙ²_ℝ`, smooth proper geometrically integral with no rational
24	point.
25	
26	**CITATION CORRECTED 2026-07-29 (`review-ajc`).** This paragraph asserted
27	non-sheafness "not even for the Zariski topology (Kleiman §2, L1292–L1302)",
28	and glossed it as: a line bundle can be trivial on each member of a cover of `T`
29	without being trivial modulo `π_T^* Pic(T)`. Both the citation and the gloss are
30	wrong. L1292–L1302 proves that the **absolute** functor `Pic_X` is never a
31	separated Zariski presheaf, using `T = ℙ¹_X`; the quotient by `π_T^* Pic(T)`
32	that defines the *relative* functor is exactly what kills that argument, and
33	L1600–L1605 in fact proves `Pic_{X/S} ≅ Pic_{(X/S)zar}` when `f` has a section.
34	Sheafifying is still the right move and the conclusion below is unaffected —
35	only the stated reason was. Full account in
36	`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`'s module docstring.
37	
38	Kleiman's representability theorem (§4 Thm. `th:main`) is
39	therefore a statement about the associated **étale** sheaf, and it is that
40	statement which is true over an arbitrary base field with no rational-point
41	hypothesis.
42	
43	There are two ways to reach a sheaf, and they differ in what has to be
44	supplied:
45	
46	1. assume `C` has a `k`-rational point. Then Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5 says the
47	   comparison `Pic_{C/k} → Pic_{(C/k)ét}` is already bijective, so the plain
48	   presheaf is the sheaf. This is *strictly weaker* than the challenge, whose
49	   curve need not have a rational point, and it is the route the conditional
50	   `Scheme.picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` records;
51	2. sheafify. Nothing is assumed about `C(k)`, and the sheaf axiom holds by
52	   construction. This is the route realised here and the one the project
53	   claims (owner decision of 2026-07-28).
54	
55	## The site
56	
57	Mathlib `v4.31` carries the big étale site on schemes,
58	`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.etaleTopology = grothendieckTopology @Etale`
59	(`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Etale.lean`). The relative Picard presheaf
60	lives on the slice `Over (Spec k)` rather than on `Scheme`, so the topology is
61	transported along the localisation of SGA 4 III 5.2.1, available in Mathlib as
62	`GrothendieckTopology.over`: a sieve of `T : Over (Spec k)` covers iff the
63	corresponding sieve of `T.left` covers étale-locally. That transport is where
64	"the étale topology on `(Sch/k)`" becomes a definition rather than a parameter,
65	and it is what lets the sheaf property below be a *theorem* rather than a
66	hypothesis.
67	
68	## Main definitions
69	
70	* `Scheme.etaleTopologyOver k` — the étale topology on `(Sch/k) = Over (Spec k)`.
71	* `Scheme.PicSharp.etaleSheaf C` — `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, a bundled
72	  `Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat`, obtained by sheafifying the
73	  relative Picard presheaf.
74	* `Scheme.PicSharp.etaleSheaf_isSheaf` — the sheaf property, extracted as a
75	  standalone statement about the underlying presheaf.
76	* `Scheme.PicScheme.picEt C` — the set-valued functor
77	  `T ↦ Pic_{(C/k)ét}(T)` that the representability obligation is stated
78	  against, together with `picEtComparison C`, the canonical comparison
79	  `picSharp C ⟶ picEt C` from the unsheafified functor.
80	* `Scheme.PicScheme.picEt_isSheaf_forget` — the sheaf property of `picEt`
81	  itself (the group structure forgotten), which is what a representing scheme
82	  must match.
83	
84	## References
85	
86	Kleiman, "The Picard scheme" (arXiv:math/0504020), §2 Def. `df:Pfs` (the
87	étale-sheaf clause) and Thm. 2.5 (`th:comp`), §4 Thm. `th:main`.
88	Blueprint: `def:rel_pic_etale_sheafification`,
89	`thm:rel_pic_etale_sheaf_group_structure`, `sec:fga_pic_setup`.
90	-/
91

93	
94	universe u
95	
96	open CategoryTheory
97	
98	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
99	
100	namespace Scheme

102	/-! ## §1. The étale site of `(Sch/k)` -/
103	
104	/-- **The étale topology on `(Sch/k)`.**
105	
106	The big étale topology on schemes (`Scheme.etaleTopology`, Mathlib
107	`AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Etale.lean`) localised at `Spec k` along SGA 4
108	III 5.2.1 (`GrothendieckTopology.over`): a sieve of a `k`-scheme `T` is
109	covering exactly when the sieve it generates on the underlying scheme
110	`T.left` is covering for the étale topology
111	(`GrothendieckTopology.mem_over_iff`).
112	
113	This is the site on which the relative Picard presheaf of
114	`Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean` lives, so it is the site whose sheafification
115	produces Kleiman's `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`. Note that the earlier
116	`PicSharp.etSheaf` of that file takes the topology as a *parameter*, for
117	want of a canonical choice; this definition supplies the canonical one, and
118	`PicSharp.etaleSheaf` below is the instantiation. -/
119	noncomputable abbrev etaleTopologyOver (k : Type u) [Field k] :
120	    GrothendieckTopology (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :=
121	  Scheme.etaleTopology.over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
122	
123	/-- The étale topology on `(Sch/k)` refines the Zariski one: a Zariski cover
124	of a `k`-scheme is an étale cover. Transported from
125	`zariskiTopology_le_etaleTopology` through the localisation, which is
126	monotone because `mem_over_iff` characterises membership by the pushed-forward
127	sieve on the underlying scheme.
128	
129	Recorded because it is the precise sense in which sheafifying étale-locally is
130	*stronger* than sheafifying Zariski-locally: a Zariski sheaf need not be an
131	étale sheaf, and the relative Picard presheaf is not even the former. -/
132	theorem zariskiTopologyOver_le_etaleTopologyOver (k : Type u) [Field k] :
133	    (Scheme.zariskiTopology.over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) ≤ etaleTopologyOver k := by
134	  intro T S hS
135	  rw [GrothendieckTopology.mem_over_iff] at hS ⊢
136	  exact Scheme.zariskiTopology_le_etaleTopology _ hS
137	
138	namespace PicSharp
139	
140	/-! ## §2. The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor -/
141	
142	/-- **The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor** `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`
143	(Kleiman §2 Def. `df:Pfs`, étale-sheaf clause).
144	
145	The associated étale sheaf of the relative Picard presheaf
146	`T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` (`PicSharp.relPresheaf`), as a bundled object
147	of `Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat`. Its sheaf property is not an
148	assumption but part of the datum — `Sheaf.cond`, extracted as
149	`etaleSheaf_isSheaf` below — which is the whole point of passing to it: the
150	unsheafified `relPresheaf` is not a sheaf even Zariski-locally.
151	
152	This is a genuine instantiation of the parametric `PicSharp.etSheaf` of
153	`Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean` at the canonical étale topology, with one
154	correction: `etSheaf` sheafifies the *absolute* functor `PicSharp.presheaf`
155	(`T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)`), whereas Kleiman's `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` and the
156	representability theorem are about the *relative* one, `relPresheaf`. It is
157	the relative functor that is sheafified here.
158	
159	The abelian-group structure survives sheafification because the target
160	`AddCommGrpCat` has the sheafification adjunction
161	(`HasWeakSheafify` for a concrete, filtered-colimit-preserving forgetful
162	functor); `toEtaleSheaf` below is the unit. -/
163	noncomputable def etaleSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
164	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
165	    Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u+1} :=
166	  (CategoryTheory.presheafToSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}).obj
167	    (PicSharp.relPresheaf C)
168	
169	/-- **The sheaf property of `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, as a standalone statement.**
170	
171	The underlying presheaf of `PicSharp.etaleSheaf C` satisfies the sheaf axiom
172	for the étale topology on `(Sch/k)`. This is `Sheaf.cond` of the bundled
173	object, stated separately because it is the property consumers cite: a
174	representing scheme for `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` exists only because the functor being
175	represented is an étale sheaf (a representable functor is a sheaf for any
176	subcanonical topology, so a non-sheaf can never be representable — which is
177	exactly why the unsheafified `relPresheaf` needs a rational point).
178	
179	Proved, not assumed: sheafification produces a sheaf. -/
180	theorem etaleSheaf_isSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
181	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
182	    Presheaf.IsSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) (etaleSheaf C).obj :=
183	  (etaleSheaf C).property
184	
185	/-- **The comparison map** `Pic_{C/k} ⟶ Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, i.e. the unit of the
186	sheafification adjunction at the relative Picard presheaf.
187	
188	Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5 (`th:comp`) says this map is an isomorphism when `C` has a
189	`k`-rational point (and `O_S = f_* O_X` universally, automatic here). Over an
190	arbitrary base field it is only a comparison: the honest object is the target,
191	which is why the representability obligation is stated there. -/
192	noncomputable def toEtaleSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
193	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
194	    PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⟶ (etaleSheaf C).obj :=
195	  CategoryTheory.toSheafify (etaleTopologyOver k) (PicSharp.relPresheaf C)
196	
197	/-- The universal property of the sheafification, in the form consumers use:
198	every morphism from the relative Picard presheaf to (the underlying presheaf
199	of) an étale sheaf factors uniquely through `toEtaleSheaf`.
200	
201	This is what makes `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` the *canonical* choice rather than one
202	sheaf among many, and it is the step that turns a representing scheme for the
203	sheaf into a universal receiver of relative Picard classes. -/
204	noncomputable def etaleSheafHomEquiv {k : Type u} [Field k]
205	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
206	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
207	    (G : Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) :
208	    (etaleSheaf C ⟶ G) ≃ (PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⟶ G.obj) :=
209	  ((CategoryTheory.sheafificationAdjunction (etaleTopologyOver k)
210	    AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).homEquiv (PicSharp.relPresheaf C) G)
211	
212	end PicSharp
213	
214	namespace PicScheme
215	
216	/-! ## §3. The set-valued functor that gets represented -/
217	
218	/-- **The functor whose representability is the project's central obligation**:
219	the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor with its group structure
220	forgotten,
221	
222	```
223	picEt C : (Sch/k)^op ⥤ Type (u+1),   T ↦ Pic_{(C/k)ét}(T).
224	```
225	
226	Representability is a statement about the underlying set-valued functor; the
227	group structure is transported back onto the representing scheme by Yoneda
228	(`PicScheme.groupSchemeStructure`), exactly as for the unsheafified
229	`picSharp`.
230	
231	Contrast with `picSharp C = relPresheaf C ⋙ forget`: that functor is
232	representable only under a rational-point hypothesis (it is not even a
233	Zariski sheaf otherwise), whereas *this* one is the object of Kleiman §4
234	Thm. `th:main` and its representability needs no hypothesis on `C(k)`. -/
235	noncomputable def picEt {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
236	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
237	    (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u+1) :=
238	  (PicSharp.etaleSheaf C).obj ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}
239	
240	/-- The comparison `picSharp C ⟶ picEt C` of set-valued functors, the
241	set-level shadow of `PicSharp.toEtaleSheaf`. An isomorphism under a
242	`k`-rational point (Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5), a comparison in general.
243	
244	The source is written out as `PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ forget _` rather than as
245	`picSharp C`, which is the *same functor by definition* but is declared in the
246	downstream `Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean` (that file imports this one, so
247	the name is not available here). -/
248	noncomputable def picEtComparison {k : Type u} [Field k]
249	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
250	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
251	    PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1} ⟶ picEt C :=
252	  CategoryTheory.Functor.whiskerRight (PicSharp.toEtaleSheaf C)
253	    (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1})
254	
255	/-- **`picEt` is an étale sheaf of sets.**
256	
257	The sheaf property of `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` survives forgetting the group structure,
258	because the forgetful functor `AddCommGrpCat ⥤ Type` preserves the limits the
259	sheaf condition is stated by. Together with the fact that a representable
260	functor is a sheaf for a subcanonical topology, this is the structural reason
261	the representability obligation is *consistent* as stated — which the
262	unsheafified `picSharp` version was not, absent a rational point. -/
263	theorem picEt_isSheaf_forget {k : Type u} [Field k]
264	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
265	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
266	    Presieve.IsSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) (picEt C) := by
267	  have h := ((CategoryTheory.sheafCompose (etaleTopologyOver k)
268	    (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1})).obj (PicSharp.etaleSheaf C)).property
269	  rw [CategoryTheory.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type] at h
270	  exact h
271	
272	end PicScheme
273	
274	end Scheme
275	
276	end AlgebraicGeometry

10	/-!
11	# `Pic⁰_{C/k}` over an arbitrary base field
12	
13	The identity component of the Picard scheme representing the **étale-sheafified**
14	relative Picard functor — the Jacobian candidate of the headline, available for
15	every smooth proper geometrically integral curve with **no hypothesis on
16	`C(k)`** (owner decision of 2026-07-28, protection I-0491).
17	
18	## Why this file exists beside `Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean`
19	
20	That file develops `Pic⁰` for `Scheme.Pic0Scheme C = IdentityComponent
21	(PicScheme C)`, the identity component of the scheme representing the
22	*unsheafified* functor `picSharp C`. Since the owner decision, the sole producer
23	of that scheme's existence gate is the conditional
24	`Scheme.picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint`, so everything there is a statement about a
25	**pointed** curve. Its mathematics is not wasted — the tangent-space chain and
26	the dimension count are exactly the same arguments — but the *object* the
27	headline needs is the identity component of `PicSchemeEt C`.
28	
29	Two of the four abelian-variety properties come for free at this level, and two
30	do not, which is the same split as in the `picSharp` development:
31	
32	* `Pic0Et.grpObj` and `Pic0Et.geometricallyIrreducible` are **proved** here, from
33	  the unconditional `groupSchemeStructureEt` and
34	  `GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isFiniteTypeGeometricallyIrreducible`;
35	* `Pic0Et.isSeparated` is **proved**, from the unconditional separatedness of
36	  `PicSchemeEt` along the clopen immersion;
37	* `Pic0Et.smooth` and `Pic0Et.proper` are the two remaining obligations of the
38	  headline, and both are stated here as **assemblies** rather than as bare
39	  `sorry`s, following the run-0067 reduction of the `picSharp` side
40	  (`Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean`). Their actual residues are one statement
41	  each:
42	  - `Pic0Et.geometricallyReduced` — Cartier's theorem in characteristic zero, a
43	    genuine statement in characteristic `p`. Everything else in smoothness is
44	    mathlib's `smooth_of_grpObj` plus the two inputs proved above;
45	  - `Pic0Et.universallyClosed` — Kleiman §5 Thm. `th:qpp&p`. The other two
46	    conjuncts of properness (separatedness, local finiteness) are proved.
47	
48	  Both residues are **true statements**, in contrast with the deleted
49	  rational-point leaf, which was false.
50	
51	## References
52	
53	Kleiman, "The Picard scheme" (arXiv:math/0504020), §5 (`lem:agps`, `prp:pic0`,
54	Thm. `thm:tgtsp`). Blueprint: `def:pic_zero_subscheme`,
55	`thm:pic_zero_is_abelian_variety`.
56	-/

58	set_option autoImplicit false
59	
60	universe u
61	
62	open CategoryTheory
63	
64	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
65	
66	namespace Scheme
67	
68	/-- **`Pic⁰_{C/k}` over an arbitrary base field**: the identity component of the
69	scheme representing the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor.
70	
71	Unconditional — no `[HasRationalPoint C]`, and no `[HasPicScheme C]`. The two
72	inputs `GroupScheme.IdentityComponent` requires are both available for
73	`PicSchemeEt C` without hypotheses on `C(k)`: the group structure
74	`groupSchemeStructureEt` (Yoneda transport of the étale sheaf's abelian-group
75	structure) and `instPicSchemeEtLocallyOfFiniteType` (Kleiman §4 `th:main`(1),
76	extracted from the representability package).
77	
78	This is the Jacobian candidate of the headline. When `genus C = 0` it is
79	`Spec k`, with no separate construction: the tangent space `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` is then
80	`0`-dimensional. -/
81	noncomputable def Pic0SchemeEt {k : Type u} [Field k]
82	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
83	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
84	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicSchemeEt C] :
85	    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
86	  GroupScheme.IdentityComponent (PicSchemeEt C)
87	
88	namespace Pic0Et
89	
90	/-- **`Pic⁰_{C/k}` is a group scheme** — PROVED, unconditionally.
91	
92	The identity component of a `k`-group scheme locally of finite type is an open
93	and closed subgroup scheme (`GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isOpenSubgroupScheme`,
94	Kleiman §5 Lem. `lem:agps`(3)), and its group structure is the one transported
95	onto `PicSchemeEt C` from the étale Picard sheaf by
96	`groupSchemeStructureEt`. Neither step needs a rational point.
97	
98	Stated as `Nonempty` because `GrpObj` is data and the identity-component
99	substrate delivers the subgroup-scheme structure existentially. -/
100	theorem grpObj {k : Type u} [Field k]
101	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
102	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
103	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicSchemeEt C] :
104	    Nonempty (GrpObj (Pic0SchemeEt C)) :=
105	  GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isSubgroupHomomorphism (PicSchemeEt C)
106	
107	/-- **`Pic⁰_{C/k}` is geometrically irreducible** — PROVED, unconditionally.

305	representability already supplies.
306	
307	This is not a proof of Kleiman 2.5 — that theorem asserts the comparison is an
308	isomorphism from the section alone, with no representability input, and remains
309	unformalised. -/
310	theorem isIso_picEtComparison_of_picSharp_representability {k : Type u} [Field k]
311	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
312	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
313	    {X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
314	    (rep : (PicScheme.picSharp C).RepresentableBy X) :
315	    IsIso (PicScheme.picEtComparison C) :=
316	  PicScheme.isIso_picEtComparison_of_isSheaf C
317	    (PicScheme.relPresheaf_isSheaf_of_representableBy C rep)
318	
319	/-! ## §4. The limit on the antecedent: representable implies *Zariski* sheaf
320	
321	The transport of §3 says the campaign needs no supplementary étale
322	representability theorem. This section says where the campaign may not put its
323	conclusion, and the two together are what actually price the board row.
324	
325	Attribution: this direction was pointed out by `review-ajc` on the §1–§3
326	commit, as a corollary of `relPresheaf_isSheaf_of_representableBy`. -/
327	
328	namespace PicScheme
329	
330	/-- **A representable `picSharp` is a Zariski sheaf.**
331	
332	Immediate from subcanonicity of the *Zariski* topology on `(Sch/k)`
333	(`Scheme.subcanonical_zariskiTopology` through
334	`GrothendieckTopology.subcanonical_over`) — the étale route of §1 is not even
335	needed, though `zariskiTopologyOver_le_etaleTopologyOver` (`Picard/PicEtSheaf.lean`)
336	would also transport it from there.
337	
338	**What this rules out.** The seam docstring
339	(`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`, "Why sheafifying is what makes an
340	unconditional statement possible") argues *in prose* that an unconditional
341	`RepresentableBy` against `picSharp` is FALSE rather than unproved, because
342	some curve has a `picSharp` that is not a Zariski sheaf, while a representable
343	functor is a sheaf for any subcanonical topology.
344	
345	**That prose argument does not close, and this theorem is only its first half**
346	(`I-0970`). Its second half — a curve whose `picSharp` fails Zariski descent —
347	is not established by any source in the workspace: the seam's original citation
348	(§2 L1292–L1302) is about the *absolute* functor, its first replacement
349	(`ex:Pfs`) compares the two *sheafifications*, and `th:cmp` part 1 in fact gives
350	`picSharp ↪ Pic_{(X/S)zar}` on these binders. What IS established, and needs no
351	sheaf step, is Kleiman's own L5105–L5108: for the real conic `u²+v²+w²=0`
352	(smooth, proper, geometrically integral, no rational point) `Pic_{X/ℝ}` is not
353	representable while `Pic_{(X/ℝ)ét}` is. So the conclusion — over an arbitrary
354	field, no scheme represents `picSharp C` in general — stands on that quotation,
355	not on this theorem.
356	
357	The campaign milestones G3 and G4 conclude exactly that (G3: `J_r := J'_r/Γ`
358	represents `picSharpDeg C r` over `k`; G4 assembles `picSharpDeg`), so they are
359	targeting a false statement as written and need restating against `picEt`. That
360	restatement is the content of the board row `AJC.picrep.etale-rep`, and it is
361	what makes the row a *route repair* rather than a missing theorem.
362	
363	**The binder check, which the earlier text here left open, now closes**: the
364	witness is a smooth plane conic over `ℝ`, hence smooth, proper and
365	geometrically integral — this file's exact binders — and it has no `ℝ`-point,
366	which is what makes the two functors differ. So the antecedent of this theorem
367	is genuinely uninhabitable in general, not merely unproved.
368	
369	What remains unformalised is the *counterexample itself* (that `Pic_{X/ℝ}` of
370	that conic is not representable); it is quoted from Kleiman rather than
371	constructed in Lean. `not_representableBy_picSharp_of_not_isIso_picEtComparison`
372	below isolates exactly what a Lean version of it would have to supply. -/
373	theorem picSharp_isSheaf_zariski_of_representableBy {k : Type u} [Field k]
374	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
375	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
376	    {X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
377	    (rep : (picSharp C).RepresentableBy X) :
378	    Presieve.IsSheaf (Scheme.zariskiTopology.over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
379	      (picSharp C) := by
380	  haveI : (picSharp C).IsRepresentable := ⟨X, ⟨rep⟩⟩
381	  exact GrothendieckTopology.Subcanonical.isSheaf_of_isRepresentable _
382	
383	/-- **Kleiman's non-representability argument, as a Lean theorem: if the
384	comparison is not an isomorphism then `picSharp` is not representable.**
385	
386	This is the honest replacement for the Zariski-sheaf mechanism above, and it is
387	strictly better: it needs no sheaf step and no topology, only §3.
388	
389	Kleiman's own reasoning at L5105–L5108 and L5126–L5129 is exactly this. For the
390	real conic he shows `Pic_{X/ℝ}` and `Pic_{(X/ℝ)ét}` *differ*, and concludes
391	"`Pic_{X/ℝ}` is not representable" — with `Pic_{(X/ℝ)ét}` representable by the
392	Main Theorem. The inference from "they differ" to "the unsheafified one is not
393	representable" is not stated as needing an argument in the source; here it is
394	one, and it is the contrapositive of
395	`isIso_picEtComparison_of_picSharp_representability`: representability of
396	`picSharp` forces the comparison to be an isomorphism, so the two functors
397	cannot differ.
398	
399	**This is what converts the route claim from a quotation into a reduction.**
400	Combined with §3, the campaign's tail is constrained as follows: any proof that
401	some scheme represents `picSharp C` over a general field `k` would prove that
402	`picEtComparison C` is an isomorphism for every such `C` — including curves with
403	no `k`-point, where Kleiman exhibits it as non-surjective. So G3 and G4 cannot
404	be proved as written, and the repair is to descend `picEt`.
405	
406	**The one thing still quoted rather than proved**: that the comparison genuinely
407	fails to be an isomorphism for that conic. Formalising it means producing a
408	class in `picEt C (Spec ℝ)` outside the image — Kleiman's `φ*O(1)`, whose
409	argument runs through `h⁰` on `ℙ¹_ℂ` and flat base change. That is a bounded,
410	well-specified piece of work, and this theorem is the interface it would plug
411	into. -/
412	theorem not_representableBy_picSharp_of_not_isIso_picEtComparison {k : Type u} [Field k]
413	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
414	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
415	    (hne : ¬ IsIso (picEtComparison C)) (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :
416	    IsEmpty ((picSharp C).RepresentableBy X) :=
417	  ⟨fun rep => hne (Scheme.isIso_picEtComparison_of_picSharp_representability C rep)⟩
418	
419	/-- The same statement in the shape the seam's clause (1) uses: if the
420	comparison fails to be an isomorphism, the `picSharp` analogue of clause (1) is
421	FALSE — no scheme at all represents `picSharp C`, with or without the
422	finiteness and separatedness conjuncts.
423	
424	This is the precise sense in which the campaign's endpoint is not merely
425	unproved. Note the quantifier: `X` ranges over all `k`-schemes, so this refutes
426	the existential, not just the pinned witness `PicScheme C`. -/
427	theorem not_exists_representing_picSharp_of_not_isIso {k : Type u} [Field k]
428	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
429	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
430	    (hne : ¬ IsIso (picEtComparison C)) :
431	    ¬ ∃ X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)),
432	        Nonempty ((picSharp C).RepresentableBy X) ∧
433	          LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ IsSeparated X.hom := by
434	  rintro ⟨X, ⟨rep⟩, -, -⟩
435	  exact (not_representableBy_picSharp_of_not_isIso_picEtComparison C hne X).false rep
436	
437	end PicScheme
438	
439	end Scheme

377	/-! ## §3. Constant-degree families -/
378	
379	/-- A divisor family **has (constant) fibre degree `d`** when every fibre
380	divisor has degree `d` (Kleiman §3 Ex. `ex:DivC`).  Vacuously true for every
381	`d` when `T` is empty — which is why the degree pieces of `DivFunctor` are
382	pairwise disjoint only over nonempty bases (`ClassHasFiberDeg.unique`). -/
383	def HasFiberDeg {T : Over S} (x : DivFamily π T) (d : ℕ) : Prop :=
384	  ∀ t : (T.left : Scheme.{u}), x.fiberDeg t = d
385	
386	/-- Constant fibre degree is invariant under the divisor equivalence
387	(`DivFamily.Rel`): well-definedness input for the degree slice of the
388	quotient functor. -/
389	theorem Rel.hasFiberDeg_iff {T : Over S} {x y : DivFamily π T} (h : x.Rel y)
390	    (d : ℕ) : x.HasFiberDeg d ↔ y.HasFiberDeg d :=
391	  forall_congr' fun t => by rw [h.fiberDeg_eq t]
392	
393	/-- Constant fibre degree is stable under arbitrary base change — the degree
394	slice `DivFunctorDeg` is a subfunctor, not just a sub-presheaf-of-sets.
395	Immediate from `fiberDeg_pullbackAlong`. -/
396	theorem HasFiberDeg.pullbackAlong {T T' : Over S} {x : DivFamily π T} {d : ℕ}
397	    (hx : x.HasFiberDeg d) (ψ : T' ⟶ T) :
398	    (x.pullbackAlong ψ).HasFiberDeg d :=
399	  fun t' => (fiberDeg_pullbackAlong ψ x t').trans (hx (ψ.left.base t'))
400	
401	/-- Constant fibre degree, descended to the divisor classes
402	`Quotient (DivFamily.setoid π T)` — the carrier predicate of
403	`DivFunctorDeg π d`.  Well defined by `Rel.hasFiberDeg_iff`. -/
404	def ClassHasFiberDeg {T : Over S} (d : ℕ)
405	    (z : Quotient (DivFamily.setoid π T)) : Prop :=
406	  Quotient.liftOn z (fun x => x.HasFiberDeg d)
407	    fun _ _ h => propext (h.hasFiberDeg_iff d)
408	
409	@[simp]
410	theorem classHasFiberDeg_mk {T : Over S} (d : ℕ) (x : DivFamily π T) :
411	    ClassHasFiberDeg d (Quotient.mk (DivFamily.setoid π T) x) ↔ x.HasFiberDeg d :=
412	  Iff.rfl
413	
414	/-- Base-change stability of the class-level degree predicate — the
415	functoriality input of `DivFunctorDeg`. -/
416	theorem ClassHasFiberDeg.map {T T' : Over S} {d : ℕ}
417	    {z : Quotient (DivFamily.setoid π T)} (hz : ClassHasFiberDeg d z)
418	    (ψ : T' ⟶ T) :
419	    ClassHasFiberDeg d (Quotient.map (DivFamily.pullbackAlong ψ)
420	      (fun _ _ h => DivFamily.pullbackAlong_rel ψ h) z) := by
421	  induction z using Quotient.ind with
422	  | _ x =>
423	    intro t'
424	    exact (fiberDeg_pullbackAlong ψ x t').trans (hz (ψ.left.base t'))
425	
426	/-- **Over a nonempty base the degree of a class is unique** — the degree
427	pieces of `DivFunctor` are pairwise disjoint on nonempty `T` (and only there:
428	at `T = ∅` every class has every degree, see the module docstring audit). -/
429	theorem ClassHasFiberDeg.unique {T : Over S}
430	    (hne : Nonempty (T.left : Scheme.{u})) {d d' : ℕ}
431	    {z : Quotient (DivFamily.setoid π T)}
432	    (h : ClassHasFiberDeg d z) (h' : ClassHasFiberDeg d' z) : d = d' := by
433	  induction z using Quotient.ind with
434	  | _ x =>
435	    obtain ⟨t⟩ := hne
436	    exact (h t).symm.trans (h' t)
437	
438	/-- **Degree side of the A2 sign audit** (rank vocabulary — see the module
439	docstring audit): a representative of a degree-`d` divisor class has, at
440	every point `t` of `T`, fibre ideal of colength `d`:
441	
442	  `dim_{κ(t)} Γ(X_t, coker((I_D)_t ↪ O_{X_t})) = d`.
443	
444	Combined with the sign convention `[D] ↦ -[ker q]` of the Abel map
445	(`PicScheme.abelDeg_app_mk`) this is the honest content of "the ideal sheaf
446	`ker q` of a rank-`d` family has fibre degree `−d`" available before the P3
447	χ-ledger lands. -/
448	theorem ClassHasFiberDeg.finrank_fiber_cokernel {T : Over S} {d : ℕ}
449	    (x : DivFamily π T)
450	    (hx : ClassHasFiberDeg d (Quotient.mk (DivFamily.setoid π T) x))
451	    (t : (T.left : Scheme.{u})) :
452	    (letI := (pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberSectionsModule t
453	        (Limits.cokernel
454	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberι t)).map
455	            (Limits.kernel.ι x.q)))
456	     Module.finrank (T.left.residueField t)
457	      Γ(Limits.cokernel
458	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberι t)).map
459	            (Limits.kernel.ι x.q)), ⊤))
460	      = d :=
461	  (x.fiberDeg_eq_finrank_fiber_cokernel t).symm.trans (hx t)
462	
463	end DivFamily
464	
465	/-! ## §4. The degree-`d` divisor functor -/
466	
467	/-- The **degree-`d` relative-divisor functor** `Div^d_{X/S} ⊆ Div_{X/S}`
468	(Kleiman §3 Ex. `ex:DivC`): the subfunctor of `Scheme.DivFunctor π` of divisor
469	classes whose every fibre divisor has degree `d`
470	(`DivFamily.ClassHasFiberDeg`, the rank-`d`-pushforward condition in its
471	pointwise fibre-section form — see the module docstring audit).  The pullback
472	action is that of `DivFunctor`, restricted along the base-change stability
473	`DivFamily.ClassHasFiberDeg.map`; the functor laws are inherited pointwise
474	from `DivFunctor`.
475	
476	Kept at full generality (`π : X ⟶ S` arbitrary, matching `DivFunctor`); in
477	the FGA regime (`π` proper, `[IsProper C.hom]`) the `properSupport` field of
478	`DivFamily` is automatic, so the `T`-points are honestly Kleiman's degree-`d`
479	relative effective divisors. -/
480	noncomputable def DivFunctorDeg (π : X ⟶ S) (d : ℕ) :
481	    (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u + 1) where
482	  obj T := { z : Quotient (DivFamily.setoid π T.unop) //
483	    DivFamily.ClassHasFiberDeg d z }
484	  map {T T'} g := TypeCat.ofHom fun z =>
485	    ⟨Quotient.map (DivFamily.pullbackAlong g.unop)
486	        (fun _ _ h => DivFamily.pullbackAlong_rel g.unop h) z.1,
487	      z.2.map g.unop⟩
488	  map_id T := by
489	    ext z
490	    exact congrFun (congrArg (fun f => ((TypeCat.Hom.hom f : TypeCat.Fun _ _) : _ → _))
491	      ((DivFunctor π).map_id T)) z.1
492	  map_comp {T T' T''} g h := by
493	    ext z
494	    exact congrFun (congrArg (fun f => ((TypeCat.Hom.hom f : TypeCat.Fun _ _) : _ → _))
495	      ((DivFunctor π).map_comp g h)) z.1
496	
497	/-- The canonical inclusion `Div^d_{X/S} ⟶ Div_{X/S}` — the subfunctor
498	inclusion of the degree-`d` slice, forgetting the constant-degree witness.
499	Componentwise injective (`divFunctorDegι_app_injective`). -/
500	noncomputable def divFunctorDegι (π : X ⟶ S) (d : ℕ) :
501	    DivFunctorDeg π d ⟶ DivFunctor π where
502	  app _ := TypeCat.ofHom Subtype.val
503	  naturality _ _ _ := rfl
504	
505	/-- The degree-`d` inclusion is componentwise injective: `DivFunctorDeg π d`
506	is a subfunctor of `DivFunctor π`. -/
507	theorem divFunctorDegι_app_injective (π : X ⟶ S) (d : ℕ)
508	    (T : (Over S)ᵒᵖ) :
509	    Function.Injective ((divFunctorDegι π d).app T : _ → _) :=
510	  fun _ _ h => Subtype.ext h
511	
512	/-! ## §5. The clopen degree decomposition -/
513	
514	namespace DivFamily
515	
516	variable {π : X ⟶ S}
517	
518	/-- The **degree-`d` locus** of a divisor family with locally constant fibre
519	degree: the clopen open subset `{t : T | deg D_t = d}` of the base.  The
520	local-constancy hypothesis is explicit (its discharge in the relative-curve
521	regime is the `HasLocallyConstantDivDeg` gate — see the module docstring). -/
522	def degLocus {T : Over S} (x : DivFamily π T)
523	    (hlc : IsLocallyConstant x.fiberDeg) (d : ℕ) : (T.left : Scheme.{u}).Opens :=
524	  ⟨{t | x.fiberDeg t = d}, hlc.isOpen_fiber d⟩
525	
526	/-- The degree-`d` locus is clopen. -/
527	theorem isClopen_degLocus {T : Over S} (x : DivFamily π T)
528	    (hlc : IsLocallyConstant x.fiberDeg) (d : ℕ) :
529	    IsClopen ((x.degLocus hlc d : TopologicalSpace.Opens (T.left : Scheme.{u})) :
530	      Set (T.left : Scheme.{u})) :=
531	  hlc.isClopen_fiber d
532	
533	/-- The degree loci cover the base: every point lies in the locus of its own
534	fibre degree. -/
535	theorem iSup_degLocus {T : Over S} (x : DivFamily π T)
536	    (hlc : IsLocallyConstant x.fiberDeg) :
537	    ⨆ d : ℕ, x.degLocus hlc d = ⊤ := by
538	  rw [eq_top_iff]
539	  intro t _
540	  exact TopologicalSpace.Opens.mem_iSup.mpr ⟨x.fiberDeg t, rfl⟩
541	
542	/-- The degree loci are pairwise disjoint: the fibre degree is a single
543	natural number at every point. -/
544	theorem degLocus_disjoint {T : Over S} (x : DivFamily π T)
545	    (hlc : IsLocallyConstant x.fiberDeg) {d d' : ℕ} (h : d ≠ d') :
546	    Disjoint (x.degLocus hlc d) (x.degLocus hlc d') := by
547	  refine disjoint_iff.mpr (TopologicalSpace.Opens.ext ?_)
548	  ext t
549	  simp only [TopologicalSpace.Opens.coe_inf, Set.mem_inter_iff,
550	    TopologicalSpace.Opens.coe_bot, Set.mem_empty_iff_false, iff_false, not_and]
551	  intro h1 h2
552	  exact h ((show x.fiberDeg t = d from h1).symm.trans
553	    (show x.fiberDeg t = d' from h2))
554	
555	/-- The clopen immersion of the degree-`d` locus, as a morphism of `Over S`:
556	the piece of the clopen decomposition along which the family restricts to a
557	constant-degree family (`hasFiberDeg_pullbackAlong_degLocusHom`). -/
558	noncomputable def degLocusHom {T : Over S} (x : DivFamily π T)
559	    (hlc : IsLocallyConstant x.fiberDeg) (d : ℕ) :
560	    Over.mk ((x.degLocus hlc d).ι ≫ T.hom) ⟶ T :=
561	  Over.homMk (x.degLocus hlc d).ι rfl
562	
563	/-- **Every `T`-point of `Div` decomposes `T` into clopen constant-degree
564	pieces** (the honest form of `Div = ∐_d Div^d`, per-family half): the
565	restriction of the family to its degree-`d` locus has constant fibre degree
566	`d`.  Together with `iSup_degLocus`/`degLocus_disjoint`/`isClopen_degLocus`
567	this is the clopen decomposition the coproduct assembly (campaign G4)
568	consumes. -/
569	theorem hasFiberDeg_pullbackAlong_degLocusHom {T : Over S} (x : DivFamily π T)
570	    (hlc : IsLocallyConstant x.fiberDeg) (d : ℕ) :
571	    (x.pullbackAlong (x.degLocusHom hlc d)).HasFiberDeg d := by
572	  intro t'
573	  rw [fiberDeg_pullbackAlong]
574	  exact t'.2
575	
576	end DivFamily
577	
578	/-- **`Div = ∐_d Div^d` on connected bases** (the honest functor-level form of
579	the degree decomposition — see the module docstring audit for why the
580	unrestricted presheaf statement is false): over a nonempty preconnected `T`,
581	the canonical comparison `Σ_d Div^d(T) → Div(T)` is a bijection, granted the
582	local constancy of fibre degrees (hypothesis-parametrized; in the AJC curve
583	regime it is the `HasLocallyConstantDivDeg` gate, see
584	`divFunctorDeg_sigma_bijective_of_gate`).  Injectivity is degree-uniqueness on
585	a nonempty base; surjectivity is "locally constant on preconnected = constant"
586	(`IsLocallyConstant.apply_eq_of_preconnectedSpace`). -/
587	theorem divFunctorDeg_sigma_bijective (π : X ⟶ S) {T : (Over S)ᵒᵖ}
588	    (hne : Nonempty (T.unop.left : Scheme.{u}))
589	    (hpc : PreconnectedSpace (T.unop.left : Scheme.{u}))
590	    (hlc : ∀ x : DivFamily π T.unop, IsLocallyConstant x.fiberDeg) :
591	    Function.Bijective fun p : (Σ d : ℕ, (DivFunctorDeg π d).obj T) =>
592	      (p.2.1 : (DivFunctor π).obj T) := by
593	  constructor
594	  · rintro ⟨d, z, hz⟩ ⟨d', z', hz'⟩ h
595	    obtain rfl : z = z' := h
596	    obtain rfl : d = d' := DivFamily.ClassHasFiberDeg.unique hne hz hz'
597	    rfl
598	  · intro z
599	    induction z using Quotient.ind with
600	    | _ x =>
601	      obtain ⟨t₀⟩ := hne
602	      haveI := hpc
603	      exact ⟨⟨x.fiberDeg t₀, ⟨Quotient.mk _ x,
604	        fun t => (hlc x).apply_eq_of_preconnectedSpace t t₀⟩⟩, rfl⟩
605	
606	/-! ## §6. The local-constancy gate (relative-curve regime) -/
607	
608	/-- **Gate: divisor families on the curve have locally constant fibre degree**
609	(instance-free Prop-class, house `HasPicScheme` pattern — the deep heart is
610	deferred, never sorried).
611	
612	Mathematical content (TRUE at this pinned generality; Mumford, *Abelian
613	Varieties* II §5; Kleiman §3 Ex. `ex:DivC`): for a smooth proper relative
614	curve `C/k` and any `T`, a relative effective divisor `D ⊆ C ×_k T` is finite
615	flat over `T` (proper + quasi-finite: each `D_t` is the zero scheme of a
616	regular section of an invertible ideal on the curve `C_t`, hence
617	`0`-dimensional), so `q_* O_D` is finite locally free and its fibre rank —
618	`DivFamily.fiberDeg` — is Zariski-locally constant.  Discharge route: the
619	finiteness/rank half of the campaign's B3 rigid-pushforward engine plus
620	relative-dimension-1 quasi-finiteness; both are outside the current in-tree
621	substrate, hence the gate.
622	
623	Deliberately NOT stated for general `π : X ⟶ S`: in relative dimension `≥ 2`
624	the fibre rank of `O_{D_t}` can jump (only `χ(O_{D_t})` is locally constant),
625	which is why Kleiman filters `Div` by Hilbert polynomials in general.  All
626	decomposition theorems are also available in hypothesis-parametrized form
627	(explicit `IsLocallyConstant x.fiberDeg` argument), so this class is a pure
628	convenience pin at the AJC regime. -/
629	class HasLocallyConstantDivDeg {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
630	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] : Prop where
631	  /-- Every divisor family on the relative curve has Zariski-locally constant
632	  fibre degree. -/
633	  isLocallyConstant : ∀ (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (x : DivFamily C.hom T),
634	    IsLocallyConstant x.fiberDeg
635

637	the sigma comparison is bijective for the AJC curve, granted the

1667	coefficient of `Φ_L(n)`, well-defined on the isomorphism class `[L]` and on
1668	the `k`-point `λ` (because `PicScheme C` represents the étale-sheafified
1669	relative Picard functor).
1670	
1671	The degree map is a group homomorphism from the additive structure on
1672	`Pic_{C/k}(k)` (tensor product on `L`) to `(ℤ, +)`; only the underlying
1673	function is stated here, the homomorphism property and the functoriality in
1674	`k` being left to separate lemmas.
1675	
1676	ROUTE CHANGE (run 0067). The construction is not the *Quot* obligation the original
1677	docstring described, and the difference matters because Quot is retained-not-revived in this
1678	project. Representability already transports a `k`-rational point to a relative Picard class
1679	over the base (`classOfSection`, sorry-free), so no Hilbert polynomial and no representing
1680	sheaf extraction is needed — only a degree homomorphism on those classes, which is
1681	`ClassDegreePinned`.
1682	
1683	**CLOSED (run 0067 r4), and the docstring this replaces was wrong on a point of fact.**
1684	It read: "A total function of that type therefore cannot be built from the Picard functor at
1685	all; it would have to invent a value off the sections." The first clause does not follow from
1686	the second. Inventing a value off the sections is exactly what a total function of this type
1687	is *permitted* to do, and `fun _ => 0` already witnesses that the type is inhabited — so
1688	"cannot be built" was never true, and a `sorry` is not the honest encoding of "the domain is
1689	wrong".
1690	
1691	What IS true is the observation the old note was reaching for: a morphism
1692	`Spec k ⟶ (PicScheme C).left` need not satisfy `lambda ≫ (PicScheme C).hom = 𝟙`, so it need
1693	not name a `k`-*rational* point, and representability says nothing about it. That is a
1694	statement about which values are *pinned*, not about totality. So the construction below
1695	splits on precisely that condition:
1696	
1697	* on sections it is `degreeOfSectionPinned`, i.e. *the* degree, pinned against the Abel map;
1698	* off them it is `0`, an arbitrary choice that no consumer may rely on.
1699	
1700	`degree_eq_degreeOfSectionPinned` below records the first half as an equation, so the value
1701	on the rational points — the only place the classical degree map is defined — is determined
1702	rather than chosen. Consumers should still prefer `degreeOfSectionPinned`, which carries the
1703	section hypothesis in its type and therefore cannot be misread; `degree` exists because
1704	`kPoints_iff_kerDegree` is stated against it, and it now has a body rather than a `sorry`.
1705	
1706	The `[ClassDegreePinned C]` binder is new and is what makes the pinned half meaningful; the
1707	unpinned `ClassDegree` would have permitted the zero homomorphism (see its docstring). -/
1708	noncomputable def degree {k : Type u} [Field k]
1709	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
1710	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
1711	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C] [ClassDegreePinned C] :
1712	    (Spec (.of k) ⟶ (PicScheme C).left) → ℤ :=
1713	  fun lambda =>
1714	    if h : lambda ≫ (PicScheme C).hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k)) then
1715	      degreeOfSectionPinned C lambda h
1716	    else 0
1717	
1718	/-- **On a `k`-rational point, `degree` is the pinned degree** — the equation that makes
1719	`degree`'s value on the sections determined rather than chosen.
1720	
1721	Immediately `dif_pos`. Recorded as a named lemma because it is the whole content of the
1722	claim that `degree` is a degree: off the sections its value is arbitrary, and this lemma
1723	says exactly where that arbitrariness does *not* reach. -/
1724	theorem degree_eq_degreeOfSectionPinned {k : Type u} [Field k]
1725	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
1726	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
1727	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C] [ClassDegreePinned C]
1728	    (lambda : Spec (.of k) ⟶ (PicScheme C).left)
1729	    (hlambda : lambda ≫ (PicScheme C).hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k))) :
1730	    degree C lambda = degreeOfSectionPinned C lambda hlambda := by
1731	  classical
1732	  rw [degree, dif_pos hlambda]
1733	
1734	/-- **`degree` vanishes on a rational point whose relative Picard class is trivial.**
1735	
1736	The composite of `degree_eq_degreeOfSectionPinned` with
1737	`degreeOfSectionPinned_eq_zero_of_class_eq_zero`. This is the direction of
1738	`kPoints_iff_kerDegree` that additivity alone buys, now available on `degree`'s own domain. -/
1739	theorem degree_eq_zero_of_class_eq_zero {k : Type u} [Field k]
1740	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
1741	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
1742	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C] [ClassDegreePinned C]
1743	    (lambda : Spec (.of k) ⟶ (PicScheme C).left)
1744	    (hlambda : lambda ≫ (PicScheme C).hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k)))
1745	    (hclass : classOfSection C lambda hlambda = 0) :
1746	    degree C lambda = 0 := by
1747	  rw [degree_eq_degreeOfSectionPinned C lambda hlambda]
1748	  exact degreeOfSectionPinned_eq_zero_of_class_eq_zero C lambda hlambda hclass
1749	
1750	end PicScheme

520	/-! ## §5. The ℙ¹ reduction skeleton (Mumford AV II §5 route)
521	
522	The B3 discharge route: push `L` forward along the finite map
523	`π_A : C_A ⟶ ℙ¹_A` (base change of the gate `HasFiniteMapToP1`'s finite
524	`C ⟶ ℙ¹`, which is exportable via choice — `finiteMapToP1` below — since
525	`IsFinite` is `Prop`-valued), then run the two-term finite free replacement
526	on the explicit 2-chart Čech complex of `ℙ¹_A`
527	(`p1BaseChangeCoverSquare` + `AffineCoverMVSquare.moduleSectionRes`/
528	`moduleSectionDiff`).  This section builds the *proved* part of that route:
529	
530	* the base-changed finite map and its finiteness
531	  (`isFinite_finiteMapToP1BaseChange`, by base-change stability of
532	  `IsFinite` along the cartesian square `C_A = C ×_{ℙ¹} ℙ¹_A`);
533	* the pushforward factorization `q_* ≅ p_* ∘ (π_A)_*`
534	  (`pushforwardFactorThroughP1Iso`, pseudofunctoriality);
535	* the standard 2-chart affine cover of `ℙ¹_A`;
536	* the **reduction theorem** `rigidPushforwardLocallyFree_of_p1`:
537	  B3-local-freeness for `C_A` follows from the ℙ¹ engine
538	  (`P1RigidPushforwardStatement`) plus a named finite-pushforward transfer
539	  package (coherence, base-flatness, and fibrewise `h⁰`/`h¹` transfer along
540	  the affine map `π_A` — the honest dévissage lemmas of the B3 discharge,
541	  Stacks 01XZ/02KE-grade, taken as hypotheses here and proved in the B3
542	  session). -/

546	open Scheme
547	
548	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
549	
550	/-- The projective line `ℙ¹_k` as an object of `Over (Spec k)` — the target
551	of the finite-map gate `HasFiniteMapToP1`. -/
552	noncomputable abbrev p1Over (k : Type u) [Field k] : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) :=
553	  Over.mk (ℙ(ULift.{u} (Fin 2); Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
554	
555	/-- **Choice extraction of the finite map to `ℙ¹`** from the gate
556	`HasFiniteMapToP1` (audit note: the gate stores a `Prop`-valued existential,
557	so the morphism itself is exportable only via `Classical.choice`; all
558	downstream uses are propositional, so this is harmless).  Everything the
559	reduction needs about it is `isFinite_finiteMapToP1_left`. -/
560	noncomputable def finiteMapToP1 (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [HasFiniteMapToP1 C] :
561	    C ⟶ p1Over k :=
562	  (HasFiniteMapToP1.nonempty_finite_map (C := C)).choose
563	
564	instance isFinite_finiteMapToP1_left (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
565	    [HasFiniteMapToP1 C] : IsFinite (finiteMapToP1 C).left :=
566	  (HasFiniteMapToP1.nonempty_finite_map (C := C)).choose_spec
567	
568	variable (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
569	
570	/-- The chart projection `ℙ¹_A ⟶ ℙ¹_k` is affine: it is the base change of
571	the affine morphism `Spec A ⟶ Spec k`. -/
572	instance isAffineHom_p1BaseChange_fst :
573	    IsAffineHom (pullback.fst (p1Over k).hom
574	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))) :=
575	  MorphismProperty.pullback_fst (P := @IsAffineHom) (p1Over k).hom
576	    (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))
577	    (inferInstance : IsAffineHom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))))
578	
579	/-- **The standard 2-chart affine cover of `ℙ¹_A`**: the preimage of the
580	standard cover `p1CoverSquare` of `ℙ¹_k` under the (affine, being a base
581	change of the affine `Spec A ⟶ Spec k`) projection `ℙ¹_A ⟶ ℙ¹_k`.  The
582	two-term complex `moduleSectionRes`/`moduleSectionDiff` on this cover is
583	the explicit 2-chart Čech complex of `ℙ¹_A` that the Mumford AV II §5
584	finite free replacement consumes. -/
585	noncomputable def p1BaseChangeCoverSquare :
586	    (Limits.pullback (p1Over k).hom
587	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).AffineCoverMVSquare :=
588	  @Scheme.AffineCoverMVSquare.preimage _ _ (p1CoverSquare k)
589	    (pullback.fst (p1Over k).hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))))
590	    (isAffineHom_p1BaseChange_fst A)
591	
592	variable (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
593	
594	/-- **The base-changed finite map `π_A : C_A ⟶ ℙ¹_A`**: the functorial map
595	between the pullbacks along `Spec A ⟶ Spec k` induced by the finite
596	`π : C ⟶ ℙ¹` of the gate. -/
597	noncomputable def finiteMapToP1BaseChange [HasFiniteMapToP1 C] :
598	    Limits.pullback C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))) ⟶
599	      Limits.pullback (p1Over k).hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))) :=
600	  pullback.map C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))
601	    (p1Over k).hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))
602	    (finiteMapToP1 C).left (𝟙 _) (𝟙 _)
603	    (by rw [Category.comp_id]; exact (Over.w (finiteMapToP1 C)).symm)
604	    (by simp)
605	
606	/-- `π_A` is a map of families over `Spec A`: it commutes with the two
607	projections (the triangle `q = π_A ≫ p`). -/
608	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
609	lemma finiteMapToP1BaseChange_snd [HasFiniteMapToP1 C] :
610	    finiteMapToP1BaseChange A C ≫
611	        pullback.snd (p1Over k).hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))) =
612	      pullback.snd C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))) :=
613	  (pullback.lift_snd _ _ _).trans (Category.comp_id _)
614	
615	/-- `π_A` covers `π` over the chart projections. -/
616	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
617	lemma finiteMapToP1BaseChange_fst [HasFiniteMapToP1 C] :
618	    finiteMapToP1BaseChange A C ≫
619	        pullback.fst (p1Over k).hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))) =

632	      (pullback.fst (p1Over k).hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))) := by
633	  have hs : IsPullback
634	      (pullback.fst C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))))
635	      (finiteMapToP1BaseChange A C ≫
636	        pullback.snd (p1Over k).hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))))

638	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))) := by
639	    rw [finiteMapToP1BaseChange_snd, Over.w (finiteMapToP1 C)]
640	    exact IsPullback.of_hasPullback C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))

642	    (IsPullback.of_hasPullback (p1Over k).hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))))
643

645	`isPullback_finiteMapToP1BaseChange` exhibits `π_A` as a base change of the

648	    IsFinite (finiteMapToP1BaseChange A C) :=
649	  MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange.of_isPullback (P := @IsFinite)

651

653	triangle `q = π_A ≫ p` (pseudofunctoriality of the module pushforward).

655	local freeness of `p_* M` for `M := (π_A)_* L` on `ℙ¹_A`. -/
656	noncomputable def pushforwardFactorThroughP1Iso [HasFiniteMapToP1 C]
657	    (L : (Limits.pullback C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).Modules) :
658	    (Scheme.Modules.pushforward
659	        (pullback.snd C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))))).obj L ≅
660	      (Scheme.Modules.pushforward
661	        (pullback.snd (p1Over k).hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))))).obj
662	        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (finiteMapToP1BaseChange A C)).obj L) :=
663	  (Scheme.Modules.pushforwardCongr (finiteMapToP1BaseChange_snd A C).symm).app L ≪≫
664	    ((Scheme.Modules.pushforwardComp (finiteMapToP1BaseChange A C)
665	      (pullback.snd (p1Over k).hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))))).app L).symm

667	/-- **The ℙ¹ engine (statement pin)**: the Mumford AV II §5 conclusion for
668	the projective line — for every finitely presented `M` on `ℙ¹_A`, flat over
669	the base, with fibrewise `h¹ = 0` at all scheme points, the pushforward
670	`p_* M` is locally free of pointwise rank `h⁰(ℙ¹_t, M_t)`.  This is the
671	`ℙ¹` instance of B3's local-freeness half, at the generality (coherent flat
672	`M`, not just line bundles) the finite-pushforward reduction requires.
673	Honestly TRUE for noetherian `A` (the two-term finite free replacement on
674	the 2-chart Čech complex `p1BaseChangeCoverSquare`); consumed as an explicit
675	hypothesis by `rigidPushforwardLocallyFree_of_p1` and discharged in the B3

677	def P1RigidPushforwardStatement (k : Type u) [Field k]
678	    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] : Prop :=
679	  ∀ M : (Limits.pullback (p1Over k).hom
680	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).Modules,
681	    M.IsFinitePresentation →
682	    CoherentSheafFlat
683	      (pullback.snd (p1Over k).hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))) M →
684	    (∀ t : Spec (CommRingCat.of A),
685	      (pullback.snd (p1Over k).hom
686	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).FiberH1Vanishing M t) →
687	    ∀ t : Spec (CommRingCat.of A),
688	      ∃ U : (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)).Opens, t ∈ U ∧
689	        Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.pullback U.ι).obj
690	            ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd (p1Over k).hom
691	              (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))))).obj M) ≅
692	          _root_.SheafOfModules.free (R := U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf)
693	            (ULift.{u} (Fin ((pullback.snd (p1Over k).hom
694	              (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).fiberH0 M t))))
695	
696	/-- **THE B3 REDUCTION** (campaign W1-B acceptance item): *B3 local freeness
697	for `C_A` follows from the ℙ¹ engine plus the finite-pushforward transfer
698	package along `π_A : C_A ⟶ ℙ¹_A`.*  Sorry-free; the four named hypotheses
699	are the honest dévissage lemmas of the B3 discharge session:
700	
701	* `hfp` — the finite pushforward of an invertible module is finitely
702	  presented (finite morphisms are affine with module-finite section rings;
703	  Stacks 01XZ, 087T-grade);
704	* `hflat` — the finite pushforward stays flat over the base (affine
705	  pushforward does not change the underlying sections over affine bases);
706	* `hH1` — fibrewise Čech `h¹`-transfer: `H¹(ℙ¹_t, (π_A)_* L |_t) ≅
707	  H¹(C_t, L_t)` (exactness of affine pushforward + cohomology-and-base-change
708	  in the affine direction, Stacks 02KE/02KG-grade);
709	* `hH0` — the same transfer in degree 0 (`h⁰` match).
710

712	when discharging `hP1` (Mumford's argument needs `A` noetherian). -/
713	theorem rigidPushforwardLocallyFree_of_p1 [HasFiniteMapToP1 C]
714	    (hP1 : P1RigidPushforwardStatement k A)
715	    (hfp : ∀ L : (Limits.pullback C.hom
716	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).Modules,
717	      LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial L →
718	      ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (finiteMapToP1BaseChange A C)).obj L).IsFinitePresentation)
719	    (hflat : ∀ L : (Limits.pullback C.hom
720	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).Modules,
721	      LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial L →
722	      CoherentSheafFlat
723	        (pullback.snd (p1Over k).hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))))
724	        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (finiteMapToP1BaseChange A C)).obj L))
725	    (hH1 : ∀ (L : (Limits.pullback C.hom
726	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).Modules)
727	      (t : Spec (CommRingCat.of A)), LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial L →
728	      (pullback.snd C.hom
729	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).FiberH1Vanishing L t →
730	      (pullback.snd (p1Over k).hom
731	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).FiberH1Vanishing
732	        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (finiteMapToP1BaseChange A C)).obj L) t)
733	    (hH0 : ∀ (L : (Limits.pullback C.hom
734	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).Modules)
735	      (t : Spec (CommRingCat.of A)), LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial L →
736	      (pullback.snd (p1Over k).hom
737	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).fiberH0
738	        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (finiteMapToP1BaseChange A C)).obj L) t =
739	      (pullback.snd C.hom
740	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).fiberH0 L t) :
741	    Scheme.RigidPushforwardLocallyFree C A := by
742	  intro L hL h1 t
743	  obtain ⟨U, htU, ⟨e⟩⟩ := hP1
744	    ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (finiteMapToP1BaseChange A C)).obj L)
745	    (hfp L hL) (hflat L hL) (fun s => hH1 L s hL (h1 s)) t
746	  refine ⟨U, htU, ⟨?_⟩⟩
747	  rw [hH0 L t hL] at e
748	  exact (Scheme.Modules.pullback U.ι).mapIso (pushforwardFactorThroughP1Iso A C L) ≪≫ e

811	  F := (Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap π ψ)).obj x.F
812	  isFinitePresentation :=

814	  flat := fun {_} hU {_} hV e =>
815	    CoherentSheafFlat.of_isPullback (quotBaseSquare π ψ) x.F
816	      (letI := x.isFinitePresentation; inferInstance) x.flat hU hV e
817	  properSupport :=
818	    Modules.HasProperSupport.of_isPullback (quotBaseSquare π ψ) x.F
819	      x.isFinitePresentation x.properSupport
820	  q := (pullbackTriangleIso (quotBaseMap_fst π ψ)
821	      (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf)).inv ≫
822	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap π ψ)).map x.q
823	  epi :=
824	    @CategoryTheory.epi_comp _ _ _ _ _
825	      (pullbackTriangleIso (quotBaseMap_fst π ψ)
826	        (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf)).inv inferInstance
827	      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap π ψ)).map x.q)
828	      (@CategoryTheory.Functor.map_epi _ _ _ _
829	        (Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap π ψ)) inferInstance _ _ x.q x.epi)
830	  kerLocallyTrivial :=
831	    LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial.of_iso
832	      (kernelIsIsoComp
833	        (pullbackTriangleIso (quotBaseMap_fst π ψ)
834	          (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf)).inv
835	        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap π ψ)).map x.q)).symm
836	      (Modules.pullback_kernel_isLocallyTrivial (quotBaseSquare π ψ) x.q x.epi
837	        (pullback_isQuasicoherent_hom (pullback.fst π T.hom)
838	          (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) inferInstance)
